433.snippet:
I recently drove to this shop to have my tire checked because I had noticed a screw in it. Unfortunately, my experience left me questioning both the quality of the work and the honesty of the service.

When I arrived, the employee pointed out the screw, but instead of removing it first to confirm whether it had actually punctured through, he immediately began working to put the tire back on the rim. Only after that did he submerge the tire in the water tank—something that should have been done first to properly identify any leaks.

After leaving the shop, while driving with the window down, I heard a repetitive noise from the tire — a clear sign that something was still lodged in it. I pulled over and found the same screw still in place, the very reason I had come in. What’s more concerning is that even if there had been more than one screw or nail, the employee never bothered to pull them all out and verify they were properly handled. That shows a lack of thoroughness and doesn’t build trust with customers.

In addition, the employee who handled my service (the one wearing sunglasses) did not seem very careful when lifting my vehicle, as he didn’t check for the proper lift points. His overall approach felt rushed and inattentive.

While the repair only cost $15, customers deserve honesty and proper service no matter the price. My advice to future visitors is to be cautious, double-check the work before leaving, and if you deal with the employee wearing sunglasses, make sure his work is reviewed. When customers pay for service, they should leave confident and satisfied, not worried.

528.snippet:
My husband and I were the first guests to arrive for the Valentine’s Day special event. We booked this experience specifically because the event was advertised as including unlimited drinks and a live performance by SWV.

Upon arrival, we were seated in a section designated as VIP. However, we were later informed that at 11:00 PM we would need to vacate our table because SWV would be seated in that section. Shortly after, we were also told that the “unlimited drinks” advertised had now been reduced to only four drinks per person.
Not to mention the ladies restroom was not functional they had plumbers there working on the restroom during a packed audience.

Another couple seated next to us expressed the same concerns. When I questioned the owner about the change, he stated that due to TABC laws they could not offer unlimited drinks. However, this contradicts what was clearly advertised. If there were legal limitations, that should have been communicated upfront rather than changing the terms after guests had already paid and arrived. The advertisement felt misleading, and it was unfair to collect payment under one promise and deliver something entirely different.

The discussion escalated unnecessarily, as the owner began arguing with both myself and another guest regarding the advertisement. Following that exchange, service noticeably declined. Drinks and appetizers took an excessive amount of time to arrive. As more guests arrived, many voiced similar frustrations regarding the misleading promotion.

The entire evening felt chaotic and uncomfortable. Some guests did not receive their food at all and were told the restaurant had run out of salmon, which was listed as a featured entrée. However, approximately 45 minutes later, I personally observed a server delivering a salmon entrée to another table.

Overall, this was not the romantic, organized Valentine’s experience that was advertised or expected. We left feeling extremely disappointed. This is not a venue we would recommend for a special occasion, particularly one as meaningful as Valentine’s Day.

529.snippet:
# Review of the February 14th Valentine's Day Dinner Featuring SWV

This review pertains to the Valentine's Day dinner held on February 14th, which featured a special appearance by SWV. As many have mentioned, the meal service was quite chaotic. On a positive note, the band TMarsh was fantastic and truly maintained a lively atmosphere; we thoroughly enjoyed their performance. The DJ also did a commendable job.

The lounge area was beautifully set up and decorated, and we were absolutely delighted with our table location. SWV made their appearance as promised, which was a highlight. The staff remained incredibly polite and composed, despite the pressure and chaos surrounding the food situation. They held it together admirably. Therefore, I give Fusion some credit for their effort.
Mostly likely we will think 2x before a revisit but its not completely off the table. Hopefully, they will regroup and move forward. We actually like the place.

636.snippet:
I purchased my car from Auto City over 9 months ago and have always been a loyal customer who pays on time and maintains full coverage insurance. When I bought the car, I provided my insurance policy, which was accepted without issue.
Six months later, when it came time to re-verify coverage, nothing had changed on my policy. However, the dealership suddenly refused to accept it, claiming that having an excluded driver (my husband) on the policy was no longer acceptable—even though they had previously approved it. They told me I would either need to remove him (which my insurance company cannot do), downgrade to liability, or purchase their own COI insurance in addition to my full coverage. I was not willing to downgrade my personal insurance.

During this dispute, I attempted to make my car payments, but the dealership refused to accept them online. They added the insurance fee to my payment portal, preventing me from paying my actual car payment unless I included their insurance fee. This forced me to call in and pay over the phone, which was both frustrating and unfair. At one point, they even refused to take my payment over the phone until I agreed to purchase their insurance. Because I pushed back, I fell behind a month, and they repossessed my car—claiming “no insurance” and “non-payment of the car note.”

The most discouraging part was my conversation with General Manager Sarah Arellano. She stated that the reason my husband could not be on my insurance policy was because he was a “risk.” I explained that she is not an insurance professional, does not have his driving information, and has no authority to make that determination. Despite my efforts to resolve the issue, including my insurance company reaching out directly to her, calls went unanswered or were made outside of business hours.

When I asked what I could do to get my car back, I was told they no longer wanted to do business with me. After faithfully paying for over 9 months without ever being late, I was denied the opportunity to continue.

This experience shows a lack of consistency, transparency, and respect for customers. I believe leadership should act in the best interest of the company, not based on personal feelings. Unfortunately, this dealership’s practices are misleading and unfair.

Do not purchase from this dealership.

1281.snippet:
I wouldn’t recommend this dealership to anyone who actually wants to compare vehicles before making a purchase.

My family and I came here fully intending to buy a truck the same day. We drove an hour because they had several vehicles we were interested in — multiple trucks of the same make/model along with a few comparable options from another brand. Since every used vehicle drives differently, we wanted to narrow down the best one by test driving a few of them. That’s a normal part of shopping for a vehicle.

After only two test drives, we were told we could only drive one more vehicle. That immediately killed the entire buying experience. We weren’t joyriding or wasting anyone’s time — we were serious buyers trying to make an informed decision on a major purchase.

What made the situation even more frustrating was the mixed messaging. As we were leaving, they repeatedly asked if we wanted to test drive another vehicle, while at the same time acting irritated that we wanted to compare options in the first place. If there’s a strict limit on what customers are “allowed” to test drive before spending thousands of dollars, that should be stated upfront.

The owner’s response to other reviews only reinforces the issue. Expecting customers to drive one Toyota and one Nissan and assume the other trucks on the lot will feel identical is unrealistic, especially with used vehicles where condition, maintenance, mileage, tires, suspension, and wear can make a huge difference.

The online reviews and the experience we had in person did not match at all. We expected professionalism and patience from a dealership trying to earn a sale. Instead, we left feeling rushed and unwelcome despite being ready to buy.

Would not return.

Review for 2015 Chevy Tahoe Transmission Service (Terrell & Dallas Locations)
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.
I wonder if the owner will reach out to discuss, if not.. oh well.. lesson learned from me.  Even though I was treated like trash, I won't lower my standards and mention all names that were involved.

When I contacted them, they acknowledged the issue and assured me that they would honor the warranty and take care of the problem. Based on that promise, I brought the car back to them expecting a timely resolution. Instead, the situation has turned into a complete nightmare.

By April 2026, my car will have been sitting at their shop for 10 months. During that entire time, I have never once received a proactive update from them. Not a phone call, not a message, nothing. Every single time I want to know what’s going on with my vehicle, I have to be the one calling them. And when I do call, I’m given vague answers, excuses, or told something different each time. It feels like I’m constantly being sent in circles with no real progress or accountability.

The lack of communication is unacceptable. When someone leaves their vehicle with a shop, especially for something as serious as a transmission replacement, the least they should expect is honesty, updates, and a reasonable timeline. Instead, I’ve been left without my car for nearly a year while getting little to no clear information about what is actually being done.

At this point, the entire situation feels incredibly unprofessional and disrespectful to customers’ time and trust. I would strongly recommend that anyone considering bringing their vehicle here think twice. A warranty doesn’t mean much if the shop takes nearly a year to supposedly honor it and can’t even keep the customer informed.

This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had with an auto repair shop.

1640.snippet:
On Monday, October 27, 2025, I visited Stereo Zone to purchase a camera to be installed in my car. Upon arrival, I purchased the camera for $303. I asked the owner how to delete old videos, and he told me that all recordings were stored on the SD card. I then asked how I could view the videos on my phone, and he said that it was only possible through the SD card.

After that, they installed the camera. At the end of the installation, one of the installers told me that I needed to download an app. This left me confused, as the owner had said that using a phone was not necessary to access the videos. The installers, however, insisted that I did need the app. They advised me to download it later and said they could not assist me at that moment because they were busy — even though I was the only customer in the store at the time.

When I arrived home, I downloaded the app, but it did not work. The next day, Tuesday, October 28, I called the store and explained that the equipment was not functioning properly. They told me to read the manual. I replied that this was difficult for me because English is not my first language. They then abruptly hung up on me.

On Wednesday, October 29, I went back to the store to resolve the issue. When I arrived, the store was closed. I returned the following day, October 30. Once again, no one in the store knew how to operate either the camera or the app. The owner repeated that the app was not required, while the installers insisted that it was. Eventually, one installer went with me to my car to demonstrate how the camera worked — but he clearly did not know how to use it either. Another installer joined us, told me once again to read the manual, and both of them walked away, saying they were going to call the owner. However, no one spoke to me again; they simply left me alone with a product that did not work for me.

I went back into the store and explained to the owner that the product he sold me was defective and that, since I had purchased it only four days earlier, I wanted to return it and receive a refund. He refused, stating that he had already told me the videos could be accessed directly through the SD card. I explained that his installers had told me otherwise — that I did need the app. He responded that the installers knew nothing about the product, then hebcompletely ignored me. I had no choice but to leave.

I would like to note that I am a woman and was alone during every visit. I am convinced that if I had been a man, I would not have been treated in the same manner. It is very clear to me that none of the employees — not even the owner — understand the product they sell, as each person gives different information. That is likely why they kept telling me to “read the manual.”

I also wish to warn others: do not trust the reviews you read about this store. They are clearly not genuine. A business that does not understand its own products and treats customers with such disrespect cannot possibly earn honest positive reviews. There are even reports that the owner himself writes fake reviews, asking customers for their phones so that he can write positive reviews on their behalf.

In the end, I went home with a product that does not work for me. I feel deceived and suffered a financial loss of $303. Please be cautious and avoid this establishment — they are not trustworthy.

I had one of the most frustrating mechanic experiences at Lovefield Auto. I called ahead and spoke with Lloyd for 15 minutes, clearly explaining the issue—my 2020 Honda HR-V was diagnosed by the dealership with a bad right strut. He quoted me over $900 for the repair but said I had to wait a full week to bring the car in. Fine—I waited.

I dropped the car off promptly at 8AM. Radio silence until 2PM, when they finally said they test drove it but didn’t hear the sound. I told them: you have to turn the wheel—of course you won’t hear anything driving in a straight line. Two more hours passed. I had to call them back at 4:30PM for an update.

Then came the kicker: they told me they did finally hear the noise after turning the wheel—but said they weren’t sure what to do. Lloyd literally said they checked mechanic forums and Reddit and that fixing the strut might or might not solve the problem. A 50/50 chance, he said. They even mentioned it might be the shock, which doesn’t align at all with what I know or what the dealership diagnosed.

By 5PM (closing time), I was told the car “seems drivable” and that if the noise bothers me, I can come fix it—but they weren’t sure it would help. No confidence, no real diagnostic work, and zero follow-through. I felt completely brushed off and left with more questions than answers.

If you value your time, money, and peace of mind, go somewhere else. This shop wasted a week of my time and gave me nothing in return but confusion.

I came here based on the positive reviews, but unfortunately, I did not have a good experience. I was charged $595 for them to replace 2 sensors and the cabin air filter. The knock sensor cost $150, but the air filter and oil sensor are $15 parts. So I was overcharged big time for a 1-2 hour job. They also told me I needed a new oxygen sensor, power steering pump, and serpentine belt, and they wanted to charge me another $770 to replace those.

I got a second opinion from a different mechanic shop, and they couldn't find ANY code from the computer when they plugged in the diagnostic reader. They looked at the power steering pump and told me it was in good shape, I just had some residue from a previous leak that I had fixed in the past.

Several months after my first visit the knock sensor code came back, and they said the sensor "had come loose," so they "tightened it back up," whatever that means. Now another few months have gone by, and the code is back again. Who knows if they even changed the sensor in the first place. When I returned and told them the knock sensor was still not fixed they refused to attend me because they saw I had posted a negative review. They were extremely offended that I would not give them 5 stars.

Normally they offer all customers coupons and discounts in exchange for a 5 star review... That is why they appear to have positive ratings. This is a dishonest way to do business.

For an affordable and honest mechanic, I would recommend PV Auto.

Edit to owner response: Am I sure I have the right company? Of course I'm sure, would you like me to send you a copy of the receipt and the complaint I filed against you on the Better Business Bureau? Of course, it makes sense that your record keeping is as shoddy as your repairs.

1762.snippet:
​I brought my vehicle to this shop for standard emissions diagnostic service due to several existing fault codes. The initial agreement was to perform a proper diagnosis. I even agreed to leave the car overnight for them to properly identify the root cause.

​Within a couple of hours, I received a call that immediately raised red flags. They claimed they couldn't figure out the issue due to "too many codes," and stated they had to clear all the codes and then drive the car around to re-generate the data. Clearing the existing fault codes is the opposite of performing a diagnosis, as it erases the crucial historical data needed to track down intermittent issues.

This rendered the diagnostic service they agreed to completely useless.
​Skeptical of the process and unwilling to leave my car overnight given the incompetence shown, I retrieved the vehicle. Upon pickup, I was immediately presented with a bill for $128.75. When I objected, asking why I was paying for a diagnosis that was explicitly not performed (they had only cleared the codes), the mechanic offered vague and unprofessional justifications. He claimed they "fixed a loose hose"—an unapproved, minor action that did nothing to address the initial codes—and then launched into demanding payment, citing the need to "pay the workers."

I offer them to perform another diagnostic review so that it may give me at least some value out of the money that I'm spending. It for something unrelated issue like the AC noise and they said that will be an extra $160.

They did not give me the keys to my car untill I had paid. Needless to say completely unprofessional, scammy and avoid this mechanic at all costs.

In a nutshell, this establishment is not reliable; they scratched my car and refused to pay for the damage. Read  below for particulars.

I got a stereo installed to my car a couple of years back and I was really happy with it so when the stereo was broken I dropped by to get a new one. First they installed the stereo but the back camera associated with it did not work; this happened later in the afternoon so they asked me if I can drop by later and they will fix it. Since I get my stuff done here before; I said OK, paid and left. After a couple of calls, I finally managed to arrange a time frame that is suitable for them. I left my car in their care waiting in the Starbucks across the street. After making me wait two hours, they said connecting the camera system requires extra work and extra money so they didn't do it. Feeling tired after waiting that long I just wanted to go home and do not want to deal with them; I went to my car to find a long scratch in my front bumper. When I confront them about it, the owner did not want to take responsibility claiming it happened after they checked out the car and park it in front of their store. He actually claimed that may be another car did it; which is not physically possible.

I have never been to a place who claims no responsibility for the damage happened to your car when they have your car keys! I called the police to get a report  to claim the damage to our insurance but the police did not show up for an hour; I was told the police can come up to our house. Thinking my time is valuable so I can go home than wait there,  I left. The police came up to my house later in the evening and told me that I should not have left the place. So I sucked it up and paid the cost of paint out of my pocket for the damage this people inflicted on my car.

If you do not want drama in your life, do not get your stuff done here. Ironically, I have got the same price quote for the service in another store close to my house, thinking the people working here are more reliable, I took my business to this particular store :)

5 STAR UPDATE AT END OF ORIGINAL REVIEW....I took an 06 Tundra to empire sound Within the last 2 years. Had a new stereo installed along with door speakers. Was told the system would sound better, but it was anything but. Was flat and had no base. I asked what the frequency response was of the speakers. The response I got was, "what is that". So I found a set of speakers with a better frequency response they could install. It helped some but still didn't compare to the factory jbl system. I let it go after they said the jbl amp couldn't be hooked up and would have to use the amp built into the stereo. As I said, this was installed a couple years ago. Lately had to remove the door panels to install exterior door mirrors and found out what kind of installation these people do. The speaker adapter plates didn't fit over the entire opening of the jbl mounts so they just found 2 holes that would line up and used drywall screws to attach the Adapter plate (cracking the original jbl speaker housing)then used drywall screws again to attach the speakers to the adapter plate, which now makes sense why I am not getting very good bass out of my system. There is about a 1/2 gap around half the speaker. I am not saying, don't go to these people. What I am saying is have them explain in detail how they plan on installing speakers and demand to see various stages of the install and the final stage BEFORE they install the door panels. I could have done this kind of work when I was 12 and didn't know anything about stereos. JUST BEWARE, and get details.
This is an update, Hudson from Empire contacted me about review. He stated the installer that originally installed system is no longer  there and to come by so they can fix his screw ups. Hudson definitely made good on his promise. Installer dynamated my doors, installed correct adapters as well as installed baffles. Sealed up the entire area and soldered connections. Went above and beyond by installing a aux/usb port so I no longer have cables hanging down to center console without charge. talked to him about a possible sub later so will DEFINITELY be going back. Hudson really cares about his customers satisfaction. Thanks, Hudson...See you soon.

2653.snippet:
I brought my 1976 MG Midget to ASM Auto Upholstery along with a carpet kit manufactured by a reputable company in England.

Karen, the daughter of the owner, gave me all kinds of warnings about what could go wrong with the carpet installation. She said they may break the seat bolts. The carpet kit may be cut wrong by the factory. They may have lots of trouble removing the original carpet adhesive and backing.  She couldn’t give me a firm estimate and would charge labor for however many hours it took. After I asked for a rough estimate, the top of her range was $1800. She charged $2100 dollars for 14 hours labor.

I would have no issue with all of this if the end result was good. See my photos of the area behind the driver seat, which, luckily, is not usually visible. It’s as if the installer was rushing toward the end of the installation and thought about how this area was not visible.

Karen’s explanation was that the carpet was inferior and that the threads can be pulled out with a tweezer. I’m not buying this. It’s apparent that the installer had to pull the new carpet loose after gluing it incorrectly. Either the threads pulled through the back of the carpet or the installer just pulled the threads loose in an attempt to loosen the carpet to reposition it. There is a bunched area at the top because the carpet is still not positioned correctly.

An adjacent piece of carpet that covers the transmission tunnel is installed crooked and in a way that it overlaps the piece behind the driver seat. I can’t figure out why the factory cut this panel in such a way, but the way it’s installed is wrong and appears to be an attempt to cover more damage to the piece behind the driver seat.

After paying and driving the car home, I brought these issues to Karen’s attention via email. She called me right away and said the carpet material is cheap and that some of the pieces were either too big or too small. The factory in England says on their website that the pieces are laser cut and will always fit, which may not be true.

It was apparent from the beginning that Karen’s initial warnings were given to ensure the validity of her “I told you so” explanations. I do understand that, with a carpet kit, they have only one chance to get it right since there is no extra carpet.

If they were acting in a way to maintain their reputation, the installer would have stopped working after damaging the carpet. I would have been informed and provided with options. I could have ordered a replacement piece of carpet for a do-over. I would have paid for the additional labor. At this later time, however, the seats would have to be removed again and I’m not sure that adjacent pieces of carpet wouldn’t be damaged during a do-over.

Ultimately, it seems that they accept an inferior result as long as they can blame someone else - the carpet manufacturer or me, for bringing in a carpet kit. They aren’t really interested in doing as good a job as they can. By stopping work to evaluate the bad result, they could have provided me with options.

As soon as I start to drive I notice a loud screeching sound in my steering system that wasn't there before bringing it in. I go back to the shop and they find my power steering hose has a large hole and is leaking air. The mechanic admits to bending it while working in that area and accidentally causing it to tear. They cut the hose where it's leaking and put it back in its place telling me the noise will go away, Although they don't bother to bleed the air completely out of the power steering system. They tell me to drive for a couple of days but the grinding noise is still there. Again I bring it to the shop and the owner offers to replace the Power Steering Pump without charge if it solves the issue. I go back to the shop later on thinking it was finally fixed only for the owner to say it's not the Power Steering Pump and that I have to pay $120 if I want them to look deeper into the issue.

A few weeks later, I was back and they told me it was a bad sensor and charged me another $350 on top of the over $2500 I had already paid. A few weeks later they changed out the torque converter and I still had the same problem. I put some temperature sensors on it and showed them that it was overheating, but they disagreed with me,  saying that temperatures in the 270' range were fine. Finally, after almost 9 months of going back and forth, I figured out it was a small thermostat outside of the transmission. I took it back and told them about it. They said they checked it and it was fine. I replaced the thermostat myself and my transmission has been fine ever since. The short of it is, While they did make a significant effort, close to $3000 on my part and almost as much on them in labor was spent over a $30 part.

My car has been here 3 times I’m in 6 months.

Started digging around some more I realized the plenum spacer is now cracked and the bolts that hold the upper intake to the engine are not in the right locations and clearly over torqued causeing the plenum spacer to crack (which is the cause of check engine light and terrible idle and misfires)

When confronted, a-1 was unsure of what oil was used and would not offer and reimbursement toward the now needed repairs. They offered to top off the oil and said “I’m sorry”

The owner has not been reachable. Funny, when I called for work to be done he called me himself to give prices. He even left me a voicemail. But now that there is a problem and his employees made a mistake, he’s nowhere to be found.

Please be kind to your vehicle and take to a place that actually cares about you and your car.

I brought my 2018 Impala to this shop after experiencing transmission issues, including RPM flare, jerking during shifting, and the car shutting off once while slowing down. I paid a $150 diagnostic fee and was told the transmission likely needed a rebuild for around $4,200.

What concerned me was that I was not provided with a written estimate, detailed breakdown, or clear confirmation of internal transmission damage before a major repair was recommended. I was also told the fluid was black, but there was no explanation given regarding metal shavings, burnt smell, or other specific evidence of catastrophic failure.

The owner was respectful during our conversations and did not pressure me to make an immediate decision, which I appreciated. However, because of the lack of documentation and clarity surrounding the diagnosis and pricing, I decided to seek a second opinion before committing to such a major repair.

I would recommend that future customers ask for:
- a written estimate
- detailed diagnostic findings
- confirmation of internal damage
- warranty details in writing

before approving expensive transmission work.

Chris seemed like a very nice and genuine guy. However, I think his business practices are a little scammy. I found his number on Google and called to get a quote for an interior cleaning for my Kia Soul with dog hair. Chris said he charges $150 and that dog hair was included. He said he could come out immediately to take a look. As soon as he arrived, he began taking things out of his van and started cleaning. Halfway through vacuuming I asked how much it would be now that he's seen the car, he stuck with $150, stating that he usually charges for dog hair, but he's got me covered this time, even though he said the cost already covers dog hair on the phone. I found his website, where it says a "Basic Full Wash" is $140, which includes basic interior cleaning and an exterior wash. I paid $150 for just a very basic interior cleaning. Chris was done cleaning in literally less than 45 minutes. No other car cleaning or detailing company I've looked at can complete a semi-thorough cleaning under an hour. After inspecting my car, there's still dog hair in the backseat that wasn't vacuumed up. He didn't bother to wipe down the underside of my steering wheel area. The brake and gas pedal weren't touched, and there was stuff left unvaccumed behind them.  Additionally, the cleaner/conditioner he used on all the plastic in my car is very greasy and has made everything slick. I appreciate his friendliness, but not his cleanliness. Look elsewhere if you're wanting more
than a mediocre job.

Response to owner: The price isn't the issue, it's the quality of work. I have no problem paying for a job well done. However, charging $150 for there to still be a significant amount of dog hair, dirt, and untouched spots in my car is ridiculous. You call yourself "the best", but I could've done a better job with my own vacuum and rags. Do better.

Again, when you get a detail, everything is fresh, so you give the head nod, you say hey appreciate it and keep it moving becuase it looks good in the moment.

Had the stains been there before my service, I wouldn’t even waste my time writing this. It essentially felt like this was something I could’ve done myself.

I held off writing this to give it a chance to dry out fully, hoping I wouldn’t need to leave a negative review. They were polite and worked hard in the heat. The customer service is there when you call but the output needs to match.

I didn't want to get jerked around at a dealership so I took my car to this place after reading such fantastic reviews. First impression was that it was a nice family run shop with dad(Joe) and his daughter (Amanda) running the place.

They were quite busy and I was advised to leave my car with them. Before leaving, I had a conversation with Amanda and explicitly discussed about no fees, or work done on the car without my permission first. She agreed, so off I went. When I came back a couple hours later, Joe found a list of problems with my car. I was advised that my EGR valve needed to be completely replaced and alignment had issues and my wheel bearings needed to be replaced as one side was pretty badly damaged. Price was quoted to me in the thousands and I thought OK, fair enough for all the parts and labor but the wait time was too long and they wouldn't be able to see my car until 3-4 days later. I had to decline because I needed to be back on the road in 2 days and decided that I would come back another time to at least have the bearings replaced as they mentioned it was very worn out. Amanda was not too sure on how to give me an explanation and Joe had just left the office, so we called Joe to check with him to see if the noise wasn't anything else. To my surprise & confusion, Joe steered the conversation into me owing them money since they had to test my car 3 times with 2 different mechanics listening for noises. I surely did not ask for them to test it 3 times with multiple mechanics...otherwise it would have been free to run a check engine light check. Because Joe made his case so strongly, Amanda backed him up and stood by his decision to charge me, even though we discussed that this wouldn't happen. They did mention that if I came back and got the work done with them, this fee I pay now would go towards the cost of repairs when I bring it in next time. Not exactly what was agreed, but I didn't want to make things ugly over a $100 dollar fee. At this point, I intended to come back later to get the wheel work done.

Since I needed to be back on the road, I took my car to the VW dealership and they did a engine light check and found a loose clamp that was causing the noise and low pressure on the EGR valve. The clamp is a $10 dollar part that came loose and caused engine noise. The dealership told me it was quite obvious and they spotted it right away. I also told them that Fix Euro mechanic told me the wheel bearing had some damage and they said they checked and NOTHING needs to be replaced, just get a wheel alignment to prevent uneven tire tread.

After the dealership told me all this, you can see why I am writing this long-winded review out of my disgust for what transpired at Fix Euro. They asked me to pay in the thousands to replace parts that the dealership told me were COMPLETELY FINE!!!!!!! The VW dealership had me back on the road after tightening the clamp that came loose at no cost. I am sure other people had good experiences with them, but this was absolutely a bad experience for me.

Second 🚩 🚩  We then waited for Leo’s friend to get off work with a sensor reader, so Leo could try to reset the airbag sensor.  Third 🚩 🚩 🚩 After not being able to reset the airbag sensor, Leo blamed the sensor on a “old” car battery.  I replaced the “old” battery with a new one and Leo was still not able to reset the airbag sensor.  Leo then had his wife explain to me that they were not going to be able fix the problem he caused and that I would be responsible to fix it on my own.

They stated that they would have to send my car to have the work completed to Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, so I agreed and the vehicle was sent to their location in Garland. Upon receiving my vehicle back, I noticed that at some point during the repairs by Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, they damaged/punctured several interior pieces of my car, including the center console and both the front driver’s side and front passenger’s side door panels/handle. When I informed the auto dealership about the damage to the interior of my vehicle, they reached out directly to Steve, the owner of Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, who at first denied doing any damage at all to my car. Only after the dealership insisted that it be made right, Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories agreed to “fix the damage”.

Upon receiving my car again after the damage repairs, I saw that instead of replacing the pieces they had damaged, they simply packed the holes they had made with a putty-like substance that is a noticeably different color and texture from the surrounding surfaces of the undamaged areas. I am now stuck with a luxury vehicle that has several obvious flaws in the interior of the car due to no fault of my own; the damaged pieces should have been replaced and/or reupholstered instead of having putty packed into the torn areas/holes. Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories refuse to properly repair/replace the damage that they have caused to the interior of my vehicle. This is likely to affect the resale/trade-in value of my vehicle in the future, as the damage is still very noticeable.

I do not recommend this company to anyone, as they do not stand behind their work and they are careless when making repairs. Craftsmanship and integrity are very important factors to consider when choosing a company to take care of a luxury vehicle, and Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories is obviously devoid of both.

4415.snippet:
I’ve been dealing with transmission issues on my 2015 Chevy Tahoe since 2021, when I first had the transmission replaced. Over the past 4 years, my truck has been in and out of the shop more than 20 times, each visit lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Despite all this, the transmission continued to slip while stopped and shift hard from 3rd to 2nd gear.
I was repeatedly told:

The torque converter was bad—it’s been replaced over 10 times.
The issue was due to bad mechanics, but I was assured a new tech would resolve it.
I dealt with 4 different individuals and multiple techs across both locations.

Three weeks ago, I dropped my truck off again and spoke with the person I’ve been working with for the past two years. After a week, I was told my vehicle had not been serviced properly under warranty. I was shocked—how could that be after so many visits and torque converter replacements? I was told it didn’t matter. After a 30-minute discussion, he agreed to fix the issue but said he wouldn’t make money from the repair and asked me to help pay. I refused, and he finally agreed to fix it—but said my warranty would be void.
I picked up my truck this past Saturday. I was told a mechanic would ride with me to confirm the fix—that didn’t happen. Then I was hit with a $510 charge for the TCM, which apparently wasn’t covered by the warranty. I asked to speak to the owner multiple times and was refused. I was told, “Don’t contact us again.”
To top it off, every time I picked up my truck, it was returned with an empty gas tank—even this last time. When I asked about it, I was told, “How did you think cars drive? They need gas.” Unbelievable.
I have messages and written statements backing up everything I’ve said, including one that reads:

“Wow, you’ve been very patient with us. I would probably handle things differently if I were in your shoes.”

I’ve tried to be respectful and patient. All I ever wanted was a properly functioning transmission—not 4 years of frustration and financial burden.
I wonder if the owner will reach out to discuss, if not.. oh well.. lesson learned from me. Even though I was treated like trash, I won't lower my standards and mention all names that were involved.

4696.snippet: I was very disappointed in the work done on my car by Tin Lizzie.  They installed custom carpet in my 1972 Alfa Romeo GTV, and it ended up costing me a fair amount of money and frustration to fix things they broke.  The worst issue was they screwed a large screw completely through the wiring harness that runs to the rear of the vehicle -- I don't know if they could have hit it more dead center if they tried.  At that point, they should have realized something was wrong because the car no longer ran because the electric fuel pump wire was in that harness.  Even worse, they didn't bother to tell me that the car wasn't running until several weeks later when I arrived to pick the car up!  It's a good thing I had a trailer and didn't plan to drive it home!  I ended up taking the car to an Italian car specialist to diagnose and fix the electrical problems caused by the short circuit and damaged wire, and that really put me behind the 8 ball as I'm trying to get this car finished.  Also, the car was promised to be done three times; the first two times it wasn't ready.  Usually that's not a big deal, but I'm active duty Army and live out of state (and they know this), so I burned up leave unnecessarily because the car wasn't ready when they said it would be, and I had already taken leave.  They also had trouble with seemingly simple tasks, like removing seats and removing a bolt-in rollcage.  The communication was also very limited; in the several months that they had the car, I think they may have called once with an update or a question.  Otherwise, I had to call them every week to find out what was happening.  Sorry for writing a book, but I waited for a few months after getting the car back to write this review and I've calmed down considerably.  I also generally don't leave negative reviews, but I just didn't feel right not giving potential customers some feedback on my experience.  In closing, I will say that Lucinda and Joel are both kind and cordial, their prices are reasonable, and I wish them the best of luck moving forward.  However, I also hope they learned from the mistakes made on my car.  Scott Walters
